results.name: Seed distinguishes missing identity, uncertain coverage and rejected recovery
Unreviewed evidence and unsupported coverage do not authorise a remedy
Recovered evidence preserves original sources and invalidates their current decisions
An in-period date does not establish covered causation
Goodwill and work authority are independent roles and exact decisions
A successor plan retains earlier authority but cannot inherit it
Owned receiving request retains exact bytes and cannot duplicate or book work
Replacement preserves original asset, independent dates and original maintenance obligation
Maintenance review records ownership without moving the original obligation
Supplier claim retains one exact package without approval or credit
Customer update preserves exact safe content and requires exact acknowledgement
Reservations create owned work and prevent customer closure until resolved
A later reservation reopens customer review without erasing prior closure
New customer content requires a new exact response and closure
Physical return requires ordered evidence and never implies recovery
Supplier partial approval does not settle the customer or credit balance
Finance matches unique credits within exact approved amount
Finance can retain the unresolved portion as unrecovered without inventing cash
Denied and read-only roles cannot mutate records
Original operation recovery is duplicate-safe and rejects another payload or role
Stale forms cannot replace a later accepted change
New evidence invalidates current authority without rewriting historical service or claims
Malformed local data and unsafe money/date inputs are rejected
Missing equipment identity cannot gain work authority through goodwill
Embedded completion refuses a changed receiving scope
